stem:
An object is suspended from a spring that is attached to a fixed point as shown in Fig. 3.1.

[[fig:f1]]

The object oscillates vertically with simple harmonic motion about its equilibrium position.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State the defining equation for simple harmonic motion. Identify the meaning of each of the symbols used to represent physical quantities.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
The variation with displacement *x* from the equilibrium position of the velocity *v* of the object is shown in Fig. 3.2.

[[fig:f2]]

[[fig:f3]]

Use Fig. 3.2 and Fig. 3.3 to:
parts.text: determine the amplitude *x*₀ of the oscillations

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: show that the angular frequency of the oscillations is 1.7 rad s⁻¹

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: determine the mass *M* of the object.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.lead: The oscillations of the object are now light damped.
parts.text: State what is meant by damping.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
Assume that the damping does not change the angular frequency of the oscillations.

On Fig. 3.2, sketch the variation with *x* of *v* when the amplitude of the oscillations is 0.060 m.

figures.caption: Fig. 3.1
figures.alt: A spring hangs from a fixed point and supports an object that oscillates vertically about a dashed equilibrium position.

figures.caption: Fig. 3.2
figures.alt: A graph of velocity against displacement, with a closed elliptical curve centred on the origin.

figures.caption: Fig. 3.3
figures.alt: A graph of potential energy against displacement, with a U-shaped curve having its minimum at the origin.
